Title: AttributeError: type object 'RtfConverter' has no attribute 'register_converters'
Description: I have the following plugin:

        plain_text = striprtf.rtf_to_text(rtf_content)
        
        # Basic formatting conversions
        markdown_text = self._format_as_markdown(plain_text)
        
        # Return the conversion result
        return DocumentConverterResult(
            markdown=markdown_text,

        Perform basic formatting to convert plain text to Markdown.

        # Handle paragraphs (ensure proper line breaks)
        result = re.sub(r'\n\s*\n', '\n\n', result)
        
        # Handle bullet points (often represented as * or • in RTF)
        result = re.sub(r'^\s*[•*]\s*(.+)$', r'* \1', result, flags=re.MULTILINE)
        
        # Handle numbered lists
        result = re.sub(r'^\s*(\d+)[.)]\s*(.+)$', r'\1. \2', result, flags=re.MULTILINE)

llm_response:
I'll analyze this GitHub issue to determine if a build environment is needed to verify the solution.

CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is a conceptual problem related to plugin registration in the MarkItDown library. The error message clearly indicates that the entry point in pyproject.toml is pointing to the RtfConverter class, but the library is expecting to find a register_converters method on that class. However, in the code provided, the register_converters function is defined at the module level, not as a method of the RtfConverter class.

The solution is to fix the entry point in pyproject.toml to point to the module itself rather than the class:
```
[project.entry-points."markitdown.plugin"]
markitdown_rtf_plugin = "src.markdown._rtf_converter"
```

This is a straightforward configuration issue that can be verified through code analysis without needing to build or run the code. The error message and code provided contain all the information needed to identify and verify the solution. The issue is about the structure of the plugin and how it's registered, which is a conceptual understanding problem rather than something that requires execution to verify.
